book_meta.subtitle_child: My First Arabic IPA Sound Book

ipa_key.name: Alveolar Sibilant Base
ipa_key.kid_desc: Place your tongue tip right behind your top front teeth and blow a sharp 'ssss' stream!
ipa_key.parent_desc: A voiceless denti-alveolar sibilant fricative /s/, channeling high-velocity air against the upper incisors.

ipa_key.name: Pharyngealization (Tafkhīm)
ipa_key.kid_desc: Scoop your tongue down like a deep spoon and pull the back toward your throat so the hiss booms!
ipa_key.parent_desc: Superscript [ˤ] (U+02E4) marks secondary pharyngeal/upper-uvular tongue-root retraction that lowers F2 resonance.

ipa_key.name: Long Close Back Vowel
ipa_key.kid_desc: Round your lips into a tight circle and hold a smooth, steady 'oooo' for two full beats!
ipa_key.parent_desc: A long close back rounded vowel /uː/ marked by the triangular length colon (ː), held twice as long as short /u/.

ipa_key.name: Open Backed Vowel
ipa_key.kid_desc: Drop your jaw gently to end the word on a clear, sunny 'ah' sound!
ipa_key.parent_desc: Short open vowel /a/ (realized as backed [ɑ] next to emphatic consonants like /sˤ/, and central [a] elsewhere).

sound_recipe.label: 1. Front Tooth-Ridge Hiss
sound_recipe.detail: Set your tongue blade right behind your top front teeth to start a narrow 'sss' air groove.

sound_recipe.label: 2. Hollow-Spoon Tongue Drop
sound_recipe.detail: Hollow the middle of your tongue down like a spoon while pulling the back of your tongue toward your throat.

sound_recipe.label: 3. Heavy Resonant Boom
sound_recipe.detail: Blow the 'sss' air across that big hollow mouth cave so it sounds deep and dark!

articulation.voicing: Voiceless (vocal cords remain open and unvibrating)
articulation.place: Denti-alveolar primary groove + Pharyngealized secondary retraction
articulation.airflow: Oral, central high-velocity sibilant jet resonating across a concave dorsal cavity

word_breakdown.note: Initial form of ص with a concave tongue dorsum and retracted root (ˤ) plus lip-rounding transition.
Wāw acts as a long vowel letter extending the ḍamma into a two-mora pure back rounded /uː/.
Crisp apical alveolar tap/trill /r/ (never an English retroflex approximant [ɹ]), carrying fatḥa.
In standard pausal pronunciation (and everyday kid speech), final ة opens into a clear, relaxed /a/.

mouth_placement_steps: Position the tip and blade of the tongue just behind the upper front teeth (denti-alveolar zone) to form a narrow central groove for '/s/'.
Simultaneously depress the middle body (dorsum) of the tongue into a concave 'spoon' shape while retracting the tongue root backward toward the upper pharyngeal wall ('ˤ').
Keep the lips neutral (avoid rounding them into a 'w' shape for the consonant itself) and drive a steady, voiceless airstream through the groove to produce the dark, low-pitched emphatic '/sˤ/'.

coaching_game.title: The Snake vs. Cave Echo Game
coaching_game.setup: Draw a small flat snake for plain س (/s/) and a big hollow cave for emphatic ص (/sˤ/).
coaching_game.action: Have your child hiss like a flat 'tiny snake' ('sa-sa' /sa/) with a smiling mouth, then hollow their tongue like a spoon for the 'giant cave hiss' ('ṢA-ṢA' [sˤɑ]) before saying صُورَة (/sˤuːra/)!
coaching_game.success_cue: You should hear the hiss pitch drop noticeably lower on /sˤ/—and 'ah' after it sounds like deep 'saw' [sˤɑ] rather than flat 'sat' [sæ]!

common_pitfalls.issue: Merging Emphatic ص (/sˤ/) with Plain س (/s/)
common_pitfalls.fix: English has only one /s/ phoneme, so learners often pronounce ص identically to س. Emphasize the concave 'spoon tongue' and retracted tongue root (ˤ) so the oral cavity enlarges and lowers the acoustic frequency of the hiss.

common_pitfalls.issue: Rounding the Lips ([sʷ]) Instead of Retracting the Tongue ([sˤ])
common_pitfalls.fix: Children frequently try to make ص sound 'heavy' by puckering their lips like an English 'sw'. Gently check that the deep sound comes from dropping and pulling the back of the tongue inside the mouth, before the lips round for the following /uː/.

common_pitfalls.issue: Using an English Retroflex [ɹ] for ر in the Second Syllable (/ra/)
common_pitfalls.fix: In صُورَة (/sˤuːra/), the letter ر (/r/) requires a quick flick/tap of the tongue tip against the alveolar ridge—never curl the tongue back into an American English 'r'.
